hook: $45 in extras while the cabinets are already empty

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of empty cabinet interiors, doors removed, counters covered in cabinet contents
scenes.voiceover: While the paint cures, every cabinet interior is already emptied out.

scenes.visual_prompt: Corner cabinet shelf with jumbled cans and jars, clearly disorganized
scenes.voiceover: This is the one time fixing the corner cabinet costs zero extra disruption.

scenes.visual_prompt: Set of 4 non-skid lazy susan turntables being placed into an empty cabinet shelf
scenes.voiceover: A set of four non-skid turntables is $24.99 — no slide when they rotate.

scenes.visual_prompt: Jars and cans arranged neatly on a turntable, hand spinning it
scenes.voiceover: No installation. They just sit on the shelf as-is.

scenes.visual_prompt: Stack of neutral cream hand towels folded next to finished burnt-orange cabinets
scenes.voiceover: Then $20 on plain cotton towels, because old towels make new cabinets look unfinished by contrast.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final wide shot of a complete kitchen: burnt-orange cabinets, black hardware, organized shelves, new towels
scenes.voiceover: Altogether, under $230 turns one paint job into a finished room.

caption: The cabinets are already empty for cure time — that's the one point in a kitchen's life where organizing the corner cabinet costs nothing extra. Add $25 in non-skid turntables and $20 in towels that actually match the new color, and the $89 paint job stops looking like an isolated change. Full list and links on the blog.
